text: Pentagon declares 'total victory' after Republicans block vote to impeach Hegseth
The Pentagon has declared “total victory” after Republicans blocked a House vote to impeach defense secretary Pete Hegseth.

“The referral of these baseless impeachment articles to the House Judiciary Committee marks total victory for Secretary Hegseth, the Department of War, and the American warfighter,” Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell wrote in a social media post.
“We look forward to ending this sham impeachment in the committee room, where facts will continue to prevail and this distraction can be put to rest,” Parnell added.

Donald Trump celebrated Republicans’ success blocking the House from taking up a vote to impeach Pete Hegseth.

“The Democrats’ attempt to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has miserably FAILED! Every single Republican, except Thomas Massie, a major LOSER, voted in favor of Pete,” Trump wrote in a social media post.

He added, “Again, Victories in Venezuela and Iran, the Best Recruitment Numbers in the History of the Military (Long waiting lists to get in!), and Spirit like rarely seen before, led to the EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot. The Democrats continue to weaponize and abuse the United States of America. They must be stopped!”
House Republicans block Pete Hegseth impeachment vote

House Republicans on Tuesday blocked an effort to impeach Pete Hegseth, rejecting allegations that the defense secretary had repeatedly violated the constitution through his handling of the Iran war and other conflicts globally.
A motion to refer Thomas Massie’s eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth to committee passed in the House, 211-204.
The vote fell largely along party lines with 211 Republicans voting in favor of the resolution and 203 Democrats voting against it. Massie voted against the resolution alongside Democrats.
A new Reuters analysis shows that the Securities and Exchange Commission brought the fewest enforcement actions in fiscal year 2026 in 35-years.

The SEC said Tuesday it brought 348 enforcement actions in 2026, the lowest number of cases since 1991. According to Reuters, in 2025 the agency brought 456 cases – the lowest number since 2008. The SEC oversees more than 30,000 brokers, funds and other financial firms.

“The new Democratic majority in Congress will closely scrutinize whether [current chair Paul Atkins’] SEC is protecting the American people – or working for scammers and Trump’s billionaire buddies on Wall Street,” senator Elizabeth Warren, who is seen as likely to chair the Senate Banking Committee next year, said in a statement about the enforcement slowdown.

A top financial regulator has warned Kalshi it could be facing potentially imminent charges tied to whether the prediction market launched new products without notifying the federal agency Politico reports, citing a person with direct knowledge of the probe.
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission privately notified Kalshi of the enforcement activity.

Kalshi spokesperson Elisabeth Diana said in a statement to Politico that the CFTC’s warning “is about a procedural error involving the submission of a handful of contracts, many of which weren’t live” and added “We are already addressing the issue.”

Donald Trump was told in May that the United States had obtained sensitive intelligence that Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia, was in a relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy, the New York Times reports, citing people with knowledge of the matter.
Secretary of state Marco Rubio shared the news with Trump on board Air Force One while the president was en route to China, shortly before Huang joined the president.

The news directly contradicts the president’s assertion during a press conference yesterday, when he told reporters “No, I didn’t hear about it then” in response to a question about whether Trump knew about the relationship at the time of his trip to China.

Ben Ray Lujan, the top Democrat on the subcommittee that oversees the Federal Communications Commission, said he expects lawmakers to call on FCC head Brendan Carr to testify repeatedly when Democrats take control of Congress.
At a hearing about an FCC commissioner’s nomination, Lujan said Carr “has been evading questions and ⁠ignoring his responsibilities.”
“I don’t think chairman Carr is going to be around more than another three or four months,” Lujan added.
Asked for comment, a spokesperson for Carr told Reuters, “Over the next two years, under Chairman Carr’s leadership, the FCC will continue to deliver great results for the American people.”

With the Pan American Health Organization expected to decide whether the United States can keep its measles elimination status this week, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention tells Reuters it will not fundamentally change its response to measles outbreaks.

“Let’s say we did lose our measles elimination status. We’re going to be doing the same ⁠exact thing that we’ve been doing today, which is working with the states,” CDC director Erica Schwartz told Reuters today.

The CDC will make sure “we are leaning in to help them provide awareness about measles, emphasizing, reemphasizing that the number one way to prevent measles is the MMR (combined measles, mumps and rubella) vaccine,” she said.
The US achieved its measles-free status in 2000. This year, the CDC has logged 5,182 confirmed measles cases so far – up from 2,289 cases in all of 2025, 285 cases in 2024, and 59 cases in 2023.
Health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, a leading vaccination skeptic, has spent years amplifying misinformation about vaccines, including the shot that protects against measles, mumps and rubella.
Here’s a bit more background on John Thune, the Republican senator for South Dakota who has won re-election to serve as Senate minority leader in the next Congress.

Thune was first elected Senate majority leader in 2024, to fill the position left vacant by Mitch McConnell. While that year he faced competition from John Cornyn of Texas and Rick Scott of Florida, he ran uncontested in his bid for Senate leadership this year.

Thune had previously been a critic of Donald Trump and called his role in the 6 January 2021 attack on the US Capitol “inexcusable”. Trump responded by calling him a “Rino” (Republican in name only) and called for him to face a primary challenge in his 2022 bid for re-election to the Senate. But the two reconciled, and Thune endorsed Trump’s 2024 presidential candidacy.

If House lawmakers end up sending the Hegseth impeachment resolution to the floor for a full debate, Thomas Massie said he plans to launch a procedural measure to launch a vote on each indivdual article of impeachment, instead of allowing one all-or-nothing vote on the entire resolution as a package.
We’re watching the key procedural vote now, and will bring you the latest.
Here's a recap of the day so far

Congressman Jim Jordan, a Republican hardliner from Ohio, has won the election to become the next House minority leader in Congress. Jordan beat Representative Steve Scalise, the current majority leader, by 106-73 in a closed-door vote to lead Republicans from January. He replaces the current House speaker, Mike Jonson, who said he would not run when the GOP cedes control to Democrats in the new year.

Jordan, 62, who currently serves as chair of the House judiciary committee, is known as a pugnacious representative and fierce ally of Donald Trump. Jordan was also the first chair of the far-right Freedom Caucus in the lower chamber. He repeatedly pushed the conspiracy that the 2020 election, which Trump lost to Joe Biden, was stolen. Jordan was also subpoenaed in 2021 by the House committee investigating the January 6 attack on the US Capitol, which identified Jordan as a “significant player” in the president’s attempts to overturn the election.

Meanwhile, Republicans in the upper chamber, re-elected John Thune to serve as Senate minority leader in the next Congress. The GOP senator from North Dakota didn’t face a challenger in the closed-door vote, as Democrats prepare for at least a 10-seat majority in the new year. “I appreciated the opportunity to have an open, honest, and transparent conversation with my colleagues today, and I am honored to have their continued trust and support,” Thune said in a statement, after Senate Republicans met on Capitol Hill today to strategize after their drubbing in the recent midterm elections.

Earlier, the embattled defense secretary Pete Hegseth held a press conference at the Pentagon where he blasted Thomas Massie’s articles of impeachment against him. Ahead of House lawmakers holding a key vote on the measure, Hegseth called the effort to oust him from office “a political spectacle” led by “one disgruntled and defeated congressman”. A reminder that Massie, a Republican congressman, lost his primary earlier this year, but has frequently broken with his party and Trump over the years. It has been 150 years since the last US defense secretary was impeached. That was William Belknap in 1876, who served under President Ulysses S Grant. Belknap was eventually acquitted by the Senate.
Chuck Schumer remains confident he has enough votes for majority leader, while Bernie Sanders says he won't back him
Top Democrat Chuck Schumer said he is “confident” that he has enough votes to become Senate majority leader in the next Congress.
This comes after members of his caucus have said they are not prepared to back him as Democrats prepare to take control of the upper chamber in the new year.

On Tuesday, Bernie Sanders, the independent senator from Vermont who votes with Democrats, said that he would not support Schumer as speaker. “The time is now for change,” Sanders told reporters. “We need a vigorous debate about the direction of the Democratic party.”

Senator Elissa Slotkin, the first-term Democrat from Michigan who won her 2024 election despite Donald Trump carrying her state, said that she will need to see “a concrete plan that’s definitively different” in order to secure her vote. “I’m a no until and unless I see that from anyone, and frankly I suggest that my peers withhold quorum if there’s only going to be one candidate, withhold quorum until you get that plan,” Slotkin said.

The Michigan Democrat noted that she had a “very productive” conversation yesterday with Senator Chris Van Hollen, the progressive Democrat from Maryland, who said he is in “listening mode” about the calls for him to challenge Schumer for the majority leader position.
Slotkin added today that the intra-party battle is not between progressive and moderate, but rather “team fight versus team flight”.
She added: “Do you actually want to fight hard for the things that are going to help people, or do you kind of want to just sit there and look like you’re doing something?”
Republican John Thune wins re-election as Senate minority leader
Republican John Thune has won re-election to serve as Senate minority leader in the next Congress.
The GOP senator from South Dakota didn’t face a challenger in the closed-door vote, as Democrats prepare for at least a 10-seat majority in the new year.

“I appreciated the opportunity to have an open, honest, and transparent conversation with my colleagues today, and I am honored to have their continued trust and support,” Thune said in a statement, after upper chamber Republicans met on Capitol Hill today to strategize after their drubbing in the recent midterm elections. “We remain united in our commitment to advancing conservative priorities, working with President Trump and our colleagues in the House, and holding the line against Democrats’ efforts to enact their far-left, liberal agenda.”
Incoming GOP minority leader was accused of engaging in a cover-up of widespread sexual abuse at Ohio State University
Sam Levine, Joan E Greve and Lauren Gambino

Between 1987 and 1995, Jim Jordan served as an assistant wrestling coach at Ohio State University. During that time, he worked alongside Richard Strauss, a team doctor who was accused of sexual abuse. A 2019 independent report commissioned by OSU concluded that Strauss “sexually abused at least 177 male student-patients he was charged with treating as a university physician”.

Jordan has repeatedly denied any knowledge of Strauss’s actions, but former wrestlers have attested that Jordan was directly informed of the doctor’s misconduct. Earlier this month, four former OSU wrestlers publicly denounced Jordan, saying his inaction rendered him unqualified to become speaker of the House.
“Do you really want a guy in that job who chose not to stand up for his guys?” the former OSU wrestler Mike Schyck told NBC News. “Is that the kind of character trait you want for a House speaker?”
